lessons: With the trend (at the 20-day extreme in the call's direction): 3 of 8 hit; not at an extreme: 0 of 3, 2 stopped. Trade only at the 20-day extreme (11 calls).
Crosses: 2 of 6 hit, 1 stopped; dollar pairs: 0 of 3, 2 stopped, both on Fed or US data days. Prefer crosses; at most one dollar pair, and LOW, in a big US data week (9 calls).
Conviction has not earned its name: HIGH 1 of 2 hit, MEDIUM 0 of 5 (3 stopped), LOW 2 of 4. No HIGH, and MEDIUM only for a call that meets every other lesson (11 calls).

Calls resting on a central bank delivering: 0 of 4 hit (EURJPY on the BoJ, USDCAD on the BoC, EURGBP on the BoE, AUDNZD on the RBA); each decision was priced or read dovish. Do not trade the decision itself (4 calls).
Targets near 1.5 days' average range: 3 of 8 hit, and EURGBP missed by 3 pips; two days' range or more: 0 of 3. Keep targets at 1.5 ADR or a little less (11 calls).

Stops about one ADR away at the obvious level: 2 of 3 stopped by one-day wicks that closed back; stops 1.5 ADR or more: 2 of 8 stopped, both by real reversals that closed beyond. Keep stops at least 1.5 ADR away and beyond the level (11 calls).
The franc is the haven while stocks fall: against it 0 of 2, both stopped on the same day; with it 1 of 1 hit. One theme, one call (3 calls).
Carrying a call into a second week: 0 of 2, both stopped (USDCAD on oil, gold on yields) once the story behind it turned. A repeat needs a fresh reason (2 calls).

weeks.read: No clear regime on the week: every axis flat on Atom FX's thresholds; today commodities up, gold down. Mood risk-off 34, the trend sliding from risk-on 57. Strongest this week CAD, AUD, NZD; weakest EUR and CHF. The Fed decides next week (a hold expected, December hike odds rising); the BoJ meets with Japan's core CPI above target at 2.1%; RBA and BoC hike bets; oil at a 22-week high near $103 on Gulf attacks; the US may lift 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods; the euro weighed by France's spread risk and a PMI miss; UK retail sales weak; gold below $4,000, down 4% on the week. US midterms on 3 November.

calls.why: Weakest against strongest, at the 60-day low, on two different stories: France and the PMI miss for the euro, RBA hike bets and commodities for the Aussie. A cross, so the Fed matters less.
calls.note: Hit on Wednesday (low 1.5779) as the euro sagged into the ECB and RBA hike bets held up the Aussie. It bounced to 1.5913 by Friday once ECB officials talked up a December hike, so the target came just in time.

calls.why: Oil at $103, BoC hike bets, the tariff relief; the week broke below its 20-day range (low 1.3964). Risk: a hawkish Fed lifting the dollar.
calls.note: The BoC hiked to 2.50% on Wednesday and the loonie firmed, but hot US GDP (3.4%) and PCE kept the dollar bid; the low of 1.3942 fell short of the 1.3880 target. Right side, too ambitious a target at more than two days' range.

calls.why: At the 60-day low and falling a week; the euro weak, the yen bid as a haven and ahead of a BoJ with inflation above target. Risk: a dovish BoJ.
calls.note: Wrong: the BoJ held at 1.25% (8-1) without the hawkish push I expected, so the yen never got its bid, and the ECB's hike talk propped the euro. It ranged 175.07-176.57 and closed 176.47, above entry.

calls.why: The franc is the second weakest this week even with markets uneasy, and the dollar keeps its yield advantage (10Y 4.99%) into a hawkish-hold Fed. Risk: a real risk-off rush into havens.
calls.note: Wrong on the franc: the pair rose to 0.8313 midweek, then Friday's AI-stock rout, the Binance hack and the Treasury rally sent money back into the franc, and the low of 0.8194 took the stop by a pip before it closed at 0.8236. The stop sat right at the obvious 20-day low, about one day's range away.

calls.why: Below $4,000 intraday, down 4% on the week, higher US yields and December hike odds. Risk: the midterms and any shock bring the haven back.
calls.note: Hit on Friday: gold broke $4,000 and fell to $3,879 in a broad liquidation, with silver down 6%, even as Treasury yields dropped. The dollar's firm October and December hike bets did the work.

calls.why: Strong against weak without the dollar: RBA bets against a franc that is not acting as a haven. Overlaps the EURAUD call in spirit; kept to test whether the franc's weakness is real.
calls.note: Same mistake as USDCHF: the franc was still a haven, and Friday's risk-off took the pair to 0.5757, through the stop, before it closed at 0.5787. A second bet on a weak franc only doubled one wrong idea.

weeks.review: A central-bank week: the Fed held (10-2, two votes for a hike) with December priced, the ECB and BoJ held, and the BoC hiked to 2.50%. US GDP and PCE ran hot, then Friday turned risk-off on disappointing AI earnings, the Nasdaq down 2.9%, a $6.3 billion Binance hack and the biggest Treasury rally since 2024. The calls went 2 of 6: the two trend calls with modest targets (EURAUD, gold) hit, USDCAD finished on the right side short of target, EURJPY drifted against me, and both bets on a weak franc were stopped by the same Friday haven rush.

weeks.read: A heavy event week: the RBA on Tuesday (4.60%, a fourth hike possible), the US midterms on Tuesday (a Democratic sweep priced near 68%), the BoE on Thursday (UBS expects a first hike), and US payrolls on Friday. Markets ended October risk-off: Nasdaq down 2.9% on Friday on the AI-spending scare, VIX 19.4, BTC near $77k after the Binance hack, the US 10Y down to 4.93% in the biggest Treasury rally since 2024, yet the dollar up for October on December Fed hike bets. Gold broke below $4,000; oil holds near $104 while Iran offers a Hormuz reopening plan; Trump says the US and Canada have the concept of a trade deal. Lessons applied: every call is at its 20-day extreme in its direction (or with the trend, for AUDNZD, so it is LOW); targets about 1.5 days' range; stops at least 1.5 days' range away and beyond the level; no bet against the franc, which is now sold only as a haven; one call per theme; and no HIGH conviction until the record earns it.

calls.why: Near the 20-day low after sterling's best month against the euro this year; the BoE may start hiking on Thursday while the ECB waits for December, and shorts in sterling leave room to run. Risk: a dovish BoE hold.
calls.note: Drifted lower as the BoE hiked 25 bp to 4% on Thursday (8-1, Mann for 50), but the low of 0.8323 missed the 0.8320 target by three pips and it closed at 0.8347, on the right side. The hike was priced and Taylor called it a one-off insurance hike, so sterling got no follow-through.

calls.why: At the 20-day low with the BoC now hiking and a US-Canada trade deal in sight; the target is closer this time. Risk: a Hormuz reopening knocks oil lower, or strong payrolls lift the dollar.
calls.note: Wrong: oil had its worst week since 2020 (WTI down 13% to about $90) on Iran detente hopes after the Democrats' midterm sweep, which took away the loonie's prop. Friday's blowout payrolls (165k against 65k) and US sanctions on Canadian money firms then sent the pair to 1.4124, through the 1.4080 stop; I leaned on oil without seeing that the Iran story could turn.

calls.why: Closed on the week's low after breaking $4,000, at the 20- and 60-day low, with December hike bets and forced selling across metals. Risk: the midterms or an Iran shock bring the haven back, and it is already down 2.7% on the week.
calls.note: Wrong: after the 4% fall the week before, gold rebounded as the oil collapse and the AI-stock rout pulled Treasury yields toward two-month lows, and Wednesday's high of 4,081 went through the 4,025 stop; it ended the week up 4.5%. Selling again a market that had already broken down a week earlier was late.

calls.why: The franc as the haven it proved to be last week, against a euro weighed by French spreads and Lagarde's early exit; near the 20-day low. Risk: SNB intervention or a calm, risk-on week.
calls.note: Hit on Tuesday (low 0.9130) as the franc drew haven money into the midterms and Bund yields slid to August lows; Thursday's AI-stock crash kept it pinned near the low, 0.9127 on Friday.

calls.why: An RBA that may hike on Tuesday against the weakest major, the kiwi, with the trend up from 1.19 in two months. Risk: the RBA disappoints again, and the pair is mid-range, not at its high.
calls.note: Wrong: the RBA hiked to 4.85% on Tuesday, but on a 6-3 split with no guidance, which markets read as dovish, and the Aussie then fell hardest of the majors in Thursday's risk-off. The high of 1.2521 never neared the target and it closed at 1.2375, below entry.

weeks.review: A week of shocks: the Democrats swept Congress on Tuesday, Thursday's AI-stock crash took the Nasdaq into correction (down 5.5% on the day, VIX to 25.6), oil had its worst week since 2020 on Iran detente hopes, and Friday's payrolls (165k against 65k) gave the dollar its best day since June and lifted December Fed hike odds to about 79%. The RBA and BoE both hiked 25 bp, yet neither currency gained on it. The calls went 1 of 5: the franc-as-haven call (EURCHF) hit, EURGBP closed on the right side three pips short of target, AUDNZD drifted against me, and the two calls carried over from last week, USDCAD and gold, were both stopped when oil and yields turned.

weeks.read: Risk-off and a strong dollar: Thursday's AI-stock crash left the Nasdaq in correction, the S&P near its 20-day low, the Nikkei down 8.8% on the week and VIX at 25.6, while Friday's payrolls (165k) lifted the dollar index to 102.2, the US 10Y back to about 4.9% and December Fed hike odds to about 79%. Oil fell 13% on Iran detente hopes after the Democrats' midterm sweep, but a Houthi strike damaged an Aramco building in Riyadh on Sunday; gold is back at $4,075 after a 4.5% rebound. The RBA (4.85%) and BoE (4%) hiked, yet the Aussie was the week's weakest major. Next week: US CPI on Tuesday, a test for the hike bets, and AI earnings (CoreWeave, Applied Materials, Cisco). Lessons applied: every call is at or near its 20-day extreme; crosses first, with one dollar pair at LOW in a CPI week; no HIGH and one MEDIUM; no call rests on a central-bank decision; targets about 1.5 days' range and stops at least 1.5 days' range beyond the level; the franc bought as a haven, not sold; one theme per call (ranking USD and CHF over GBP over EUR, and JPY over AUD); and the one carried-over call, EURGBP, has a fresh reason, the BoE's hike now done.

calls.why: At its 20- and 60-day low after a 1.8% fall: the Aussie was the weakest major even with an RBA hike, and the yen draws haven money while tech stocks slide, with the BoJ's minutes hawkish. Risk: a relief rally in stocks or a hot US CPI that weakens the yen.

The franc as the haven it proved again last week, sitting on the 20-day low at 1.0941; sterling slipped even on the BoE's hike, with Taylor calling it a one-off. Risk: the BoE hawks (Pill, Greene) lift sterling, or calm returns.

Near the 20- and 60-day low: the BoE has now hiked and its chief economist says one hike is unlikely to be enough, while the ECB waits and French politics weigh on the euro. Risk: weak UK data, and it held above 0.8320 all last week.

The only dollar call: payrolls gave the dollar its best day since June, a December Fed hike is about 79% priced, and the euro sits near its 20- and 60-day low of 1.1110. Risk: a soft CPI on Tuesday knocks the hike bets.
